thesis: Genpact (NYSE: G), process and AI-enabled operations services. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-06). Net revenues Q3 1,385.4M vs 1,291.3M (+7.3%); 9M 4,024.9M vs 3,760.6M (+7.0%); income from operations 9M 602.5M vs 554.7M (+8.6%); 9M NI 445.4M vs 409.4M (+8.8%). TTM (USD millions): NI 588.5; OCF 428.7 (812.9+142.0-526.2); PP&E capex 72.2; FCF 356.5; SBC 105.4; FCF after SBC 251.1. Payments for internally generated intangibles (24.9M in 9M26 vs 6.1M) are excluded from capex and would lower FCF about 19M on 9M basis. Close 40.84 (2026-11-19) x 167,227,005 shares (balance sheet 2026-09-30, point in time, cover count not used) = 6.83B = 11.6x TTM NI; FCF yield 5.2% (3.7% after SBC). Debt: current 26.2M + long term 1,148.0M = 1,174.2M vs cash 499.1M (down from 853.8M; 369.9M debt repaid in 9M), net debt about 0.68B; dividend 0.1875 per quarter (94.8M paid 9M26). Possible market view: AI disrupts offshore business process work; the numbers show 7% growth and margin expansion, but cash conversion has stalled. Price implies roughly flat earnings; differing evidence is steady growth, offset by receivables.
counterthesis: 9M OCF was only 142.0M vs 526.2M because receivables rose 405.8M (vs 80.3M) from an ERP implementation that delayed invoicing and collection per MD&A; if this is timing it reverses, if it is credit or dispute quality it does not, and the allowance for credit losses charge rose to 22.6M from 18.2M. TTM FCF of 357M is 5.2% yield, much below TTM NI. Prepaid and other assets rose 149.9M. Share based compensation is high (79.9M 9M, up 25%). Services demand could be hit by AI automation of customer work and client concentration (not read). Cash fell 355M; headcount and wage inflation risk to margins; peers (EXLS, WNS, ACN, CTSH) and own history not compared.
invalidation: Invalidated if receivables and days sales outstanding do not normalize within two quarters, if revenue growth drops below low single digits, if operating margin gives back the 2026 gains, or if credit losses rise materially.
